blocks.text: Every practical paper ends the same way: 'a colourless gas was evolved which turned limewater milky'. Examiners never say which gas it is, because they expect you to know the tests. Learn about ten of them and a whole section of the paper becomes free marks.

blocks.markdown:
## Preparing a gas in the laboratory

Almost every laboratory gas preparation follows the same three decisions.

1. **Choose reagents** that give the gas from a convenient reaction, usually a solid plus a liquid so the reaction can be started and stopped.
2. **Dry the gas** by passing it through a suitable drying agent. Concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid dries most gases, but never ammonia, which reacts with it. Ammonia is dried with quicklime, calcium oxide.
3. **Collect the gas** by the method its density and solubility allow.

rows: Insoluble or slightly soluble in water
Upward delivery into an upright jar (downward displacement of air)
Soluble and less dense than air
Downward delivery into an inverted jar (upward displacement of air)
Needs to be perfectly dry and pure
Through a drying tower, then by displacement of air

## The common gases

The table below is the core of this subtopic. The equations are written the way an examiner expects to see them.

rows: Burns with a pop sound when a lighted splint is applied
Turns limewater milky; the milkiness clears in excess gas
Turns damp red litmus blue; gives dense white fumes with HCl
Dense white fumes with ammonia; turns damp blue litmus red
Greenish-yellow gas that bleaches damp litmus paper
Choking smell; turns acidified dichromate from orange to green

blocks.title: Two tests that look alike
blocks.text: Carbon dioxide and sulphur(IV) oxide both turn limewater milky, so limewater alone cannot separate them. Use acidified potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI): sulphur(IV) oxide is a reducing agent and turns it from orange to green, while carbon dioxide leaves it orange.

blocks.title: Identifying an unknown gas
blocks.prompt: A colourless gas X has a choking smell. It turns damp blue litmus paper red, decolourises acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) solution, and turns limewater milky. Identify X and justify each observation.

steps.text: The gas is acidic, since it turns damp blue litmus red. That rules out ammonia, hydrogen and oxygen straight away.
It turns limewater milky, so it is either carbon dioxide or sulphur(IV) oxide. Both give an insoluble sulphite or carbonate with calcium hydroxide.

It decolourises acidified KMnO4. Carbon dioxide has no reducing power, so it cannot do this. Sulphur(IV) oxide is a good reducing agent and is oxidised to sulphate while manganese is reduced from +7 to +2, removing the purple colour.
The choking smell confirms it, since carbon dioxide is odourless.
X is sulphur(IV) oxide, SO2. With limewater: SO2 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaSO3 + H2O, and the white CaSO3 causes the milkiness.

blocks.markdown:
## Compounds that matter industrially

### Tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid — the Contact process

Sulphur is burnt to SO2, which is oxidised over vanadium(V) oxide at about 450 degrees Celsius and 2 atmospheres:

2SO2 + O2 <=> 2SO3

The SO3 is absorbed in concentrated acid to give oleum, which is then diluted. It is never absorbed directly in water because the reaction produces a dense, uncontrollable mist of acid.

### Ammonia — the Haber process

N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3 over iron at about 450 degrees Celsius and 200 atmospheres. Most of the ammonia is oxidised to trioxonitrate(V) acid or converted straight into fertilisers such as ammonium sulphate and urea.

### Trioxonitrate(V) acid — the Ostwald process

Ammonia is catalytically oxidised over platinum to NO, which becomes NO2 in air and dissolves in water to give HNO3.

items: **Acid rain** forms when SO2 and NO2 from burning fossil fuels dissolve in rainwater to give tetraoxosulphate(VI) and trioxonitrate(V) acids, which corrode buildings and acidify rivers.
**Carbon monoxide** is a colourless, odourless, neutral gas from incomplete combustion; it binds to haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does, which is why generators must never be run indoors.
**Ozone** in the upper atmosphere absorbs ultraviolet radiation, and is depleted by chlorofluorocarbons.
**Carbon dioxide** is a greenhouse gas, but is also the raw material of photosynthesis.

blocks.title: Write the observation, not the conclusion
blocks.text: In a test question the mark is for the observation and the inference together. Write 'limewater turns milky, so carbon dioxide is present', not just 'carbon dioxide'. Where a gas is coloured or has a smell, say so: chlorine is greenish-yellow, nitrogen(IV) oxide reddish-brown, and hydrogen sulphide smells of rotten eggs.

points: Gases are collected over water if insoluble, by upward delivery if dense and soluble, and by downward delivery if less dense than air.
Concentrated H2SO4 dries most gases but not ammonia, which is dried over quicklime.
Hydrogen pops, oxygen relights a glowing splint, and carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.
Ammonia is the only common alkaline gas and turns damp red litmus blue.
SO2 and CO2 both turn limewater milky, but only SO2 reduces acidified dichromate from orange to green.
The Contact, Haber and Ostwald processes make tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, ammonia and trioxonitrate(V) acid respectively.
SO2 and NO2 released from fuels are the cause of acid rain.
